- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.3) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward → reduce forecast bias by 5–10% below model output.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 85), model often overshoots → apply downward drag of 3–8% to next 3–5 periods.  
- If sentiment turns positive after a downtrend, model fails to react → delay mean reversion until sentiment stabilizes (wait 2–3 periods).  
- Model underestimates true mean in bearish sentiment → add 2–5% to forecast if sentiment < -0.4 for 3+ consecutive days.  
- Forecast horizon 30d: model often lags true trend by 1–3 days → adjust by adding 1–2% to forecast if sentiment is trending upward.  
- If sentiment is neutral or weak (avg ~0), model overfits recent noise → smooth forecast by averaging last 5–7 values.
